newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks likely to waver weakly after holiday.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks likely to waver weakly after holiday.

text.p: Tokyo stocks are likely to waver weakly on Friday with the trading session sandwiched between a national holiday on Thursday and the weekend, brokers said. Hints of weakness on Wall Street may dampen activity, they added.
On Wednesday, the key Nikkei 225 average lost 167.70 points, or 0.80 percent, to finish at 20,870.83. Its December futures shed 120 points to land at 20,910.
"The market didn't react to the Dow's rises, but sentiment is not too good and it may decide to react to the weakness," Yasuo Ueki, general manager at Nikko Securities said.
Market sources estimated that today's trading will range between 20,700 and 21,050.
Koichi Ayabe at Hinode Securities equities department said on top of the faltering Dow, the approaching margin trade deadlines may become a burden for the market because of the subdued trade.

Brokers said JR West, which listed earlier in the week, was likely to attract attention as many investors were backing off from major issues until the market atmosphere brightens. They said that smaller issues as well as over-the-counter stocks were likely to be the centre of trade for now.
